title: Scalable high-molecular weight DNA extraction for long-read sequencing
author: Ashley Jones
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bnjhmcj6
materials: Quantify the DNA on a Nanodrop and a Qubit fluorometer (dsDNA broad-range assay) (both instruments from Thermo Fisher Scientific). The DNA is still crude and will likely have other contaminants present. For Nanodrop, use 1 μL. As the DNA is crude, it may give a large over-estimation of concentration. Qubit fluorometer is the most reliable. However, it is highly dependent on the accuracy of the amount pipetted. Use 2 μL when sample is plentiful. Using 1 μL is prone to pipetting errors. For pure DNA, Nanodrop:Qubit is 1:1, 260/280 is 1.8 and 260/230 is 2.0. DNA yield can be 20-500 µg.

Quantify the DNA on a Nanodrop and a Qubit fluorometer (dsDNA broad-range assay) (both instruments from Thermo Fisher Scientific). The DNA should be pure, free of contaminants. For Nanodrop, use 1 μL. Qubit fluorometer is highly dependent on the accuracy of the amount pipetted. Use 2 μL when sample is plentiful. Using 1 μL is prone to pipetting errors. For pure DNA, Nanodrop:Qubit is 1:1, 260/280 is 1.8 and 260/230 is 2.0. Expect 20-30% recovery relative to total input (~6-9 µg out of 30 µg).

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Reagents
steps.instruction: Set up the necessary environment and reagents for the extraction.

substeps.instruction: Set a water bath (or equivalent) to 55°C (range 50-60°C).

Prepare fresh lysis buffer on the day of use; heat at 55°C in the water bath until clear and ready for use. (Note: Use EGTA for wheat or soft plant tissues with high endogenous DNases; use EDTA for others).
Verify sufficient quantities of 5 M potassium acetate, binding buffer, and Sera-Mag beads.

steps.title: Sample Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the biological sample based on the source material.

substeps.instruction: For bacteria cultures: Pellet cells in a 2 mL tube or 50 mL Falcon tube by centrifuging at 5,000 rcf for 10 min at room temperature and discard growth medium. Skip the grinding step.
For tissue: Grind tissue to a fine powder while keeping it frozen with liquid nitrogen.
Optional: For samples likely to have high sugars, oils, or endogenous chemicals (e.g., plant tissue), perform a sorbitol wash according to Jones and Schwessinger (2020).

steps.title: Lysis and Enzymatic Digestion
steps.instruction: Lyse the cells and degrade proteins and RNA.

substeps.instruction: Add lysis buffer to tissue (1-2x the approximate volume of ground tissue). Vortex or shake vigorously to mix.
For bacteria cultures: Add lysozyme at approximately 2-4 mg/mL.
Add RNAse A and Proteinase K (both recommended at 50-100 µg/mL) to the solution and mix by swirling and inverting. (Note: For bacteria, do not add Proteinase K yet).
Incubate samples at 55°C, shaking at ~450 rpm if possible.
For bacteria cultures: Add Proteinase K and incubate at 55°C for an additional 30 min.

steps.title: Homogenate Processing
steps.instruction: Filter and aliquot the homogenate for large-scale preparations.

substeps.instruction: For large preps only: Filter the homogenate using a sieve or disk membrane mesh in a funnel into a 250 mL Schott bottle, squeezing out residual homogenate. Split the homogenate into 50 mL Falcon tubes, with 20 mL per tube.
Add 1/3 volume of 5 M Potassium Acetate (Lysis buffer volumes: Small=1.2 mL, Medium=10 mL, Large=125 mL) and mix by inverting.
Incubate on ice (4°C) for 10 min without rotation.
Centrifuge at 5,000 rcf for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer supernatant to a new tube and centrifuge again at 5,000 rcf for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a final new tube.

steps.title: DNA Binding and Bead Purification
steps.instruction: Bind DNA to magnetic beads and wash to remove impurities.

substeps.instruction: Add approximately an equal volume (or more) of binding buffer to the supernatant.
Add thoroughly mixed 2% Sera-Mag beads to the sample.
Mix by inverting the tube 20 times, then incubate with gentle mixing (rotator or shaker) at room temperature.
Place the tube in a magnetic rack until the solution is clear.
Remove the supernatant without disturbing the beads.
Wash the beads by filling the tube with 70% ethanol, letting them settle, and decanting. Repeat 2 more times (or until clean). If beads are very dirty, resuspend by flicking before magnetizing.

steps.title: Bead Transfer and Drying
steps.instruction: Consolidate beads for medium/large preps and prepare for elution.

substeps.instruction: For medium and large preps: Transfer beads to a 2 mL Eppendorf tube by adding 1 mL of 70% ethanol to dislodge them; repeat with another 1 mL if necessary. Keep beads wet with ethanol throughout.
Remove all traces of ethanol and air dry the beads for 1-4 min. Do not let beads dry completely.

steps.title: DNA Elution
steps.instruction: Elute the DNA from the magnetic beads.

substeps.instruction: Remove tube from magnetic rack and add 10 mM TRIS-HCl pH 8 (or nuclease-free water). Gently resuspend by tapping or using a wide-bore pipette tip.
Incubate at room temperature for at least 10 min.
Place in magnetic rack until the solution is clear.
Transfer the supernatant (DNA) to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube (preferably DNA LoBind).
Perform a second elution using the same volume of buffer/water; resuspend, incubate, magnetize, and transfer to a separate 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Storage and Quality Assessment
steps.instruction: Store the DNA and determine if further purification is needed.

substeps.instruction: Store DNA at 4°C to prevent shearing from freeze-thaw cycles.
If DNA is crude (especially plant samples), consider DNA clean-up or size selection. If discolored, perform DNA clean-up before using a Short-Read Eliminator kit.
If a precipitant is visible, briefly spin down and take the upper aqueous layer for further purification.

steps.title: Optional Gel Purification (Pippin Prep)
steps.instruction: Perform automated electrophoresis for recalcitrant plant samples.

substeps.instruction: Gel purify approximately 30 µg of DNA using a PippinHT (or equivalent). Use a 20 kb high pass separation (or 15 kb if DNA is limited).
Load 20 µL of DNA per lane (up to 3 µg per lane). Use a chloroform:isoamyl alcohol 24:1 clean-up first if the sample is very dirty.
After separation, wait at least 45 min (up to overnight) to aid recovery.
Collect elution well contents into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube (approx. 300 µL).
Add 30 µL of 0.1% tween in electrophoresis buffer to each elution well, wait 5 min, and transfer to the same tube (total volume approx. 600 µL).

steps.title: Final Bead Clean-up after Gel Purification
steps.instruction: Perform a final bead-based purification of the gel-eluted DNA.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.2x binding buffer (approx. 720 µL) and 100 µL of 2% Sera-Mag beads to the tube. Incubate 5-10 min at room temperature.
Place on magnetic rack for 5 min until clear and discard supernatant.
Wash beads twice with 1 mL freshly prepared 70% ethanol.
Air dry beads for 1-4 min (do not dry completely).
Remove from rack and elute with 50 µL of nuclease-free water. Incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Place on magnetic rack for 5 min until clear and transfer DNA to a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube (preferably DNA LoBind) using a wide-bore tip.
Perform a second elution with the same volume and store in a separate 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
